title: Weak-equivalence comparisons for cofibrant colimit constructions
statement:
Let $\mathcal M$ be a model category in the sense of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], with all small limits and colimits; smallness is relative to fixed universes, which may be enlarged. The following colimit comparison assertions hold.

(a) A small coproduct of weak equivalences between cofibrant objects is a weak equivalence, and these coproducts are cofibrant.

(b) Given a map of spans $(X\leftarrow A\xrightarrow{i}B)\to(X'\leftarrow A'\xrightarrow{i'}B')$, assume all six objects are cofibrant, $i,i'$ are cofibrations, and the three component maps are weak equivalences. Then the induced map $X\amalg_A B\to X'\amalg_{A'}B'$ is a weak equivalence, and both pushouts are cofibrant.

(c) Let $\theta$ be a small nonzero limit ordinal. Let $(X_\alpha)_{\alpha<\theta}$ and $(Y_\alpha)_{\alpha<\theta}$ be ordinal-indexed diagrams with cofibrant initial objects, cofibration successor maps, and colimit cocones at every nonzero limit ordinal less than $\theta$. Every natural transformation $u_\alpha:X_\alpha\to Y_\alpha$ whose components are weak equivalences induces a weak equivalence $\operatorname{colim}_{\alpha<\theta}X_\alpha\to\operatorname{colim}_{\alpha<\theta}Y_\alpha$; both colimits are cofibrant. No properness hypothesis on $\mathcal M$ is imposed.

external.document: Mark Hovey, Model categories, https://ericmalm.net/ac/projects/symmetric-spectra/hovey--model-cats.pdf (read online; not archived in literature/)
external.place: Definition 5.1.1, Theorem 5.1.3 and Corollary 5.1.6 (discrete and ordinal direct categories), and Lemma 5.2.6 (cube lemma).

proof.text: Use the model-category classes $C,F,W$ and cofibrancy convention of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. For every small indexing category $J$, the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives $\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{colim}_J D,T)=\operatorname{Nat}(D,\operatorname{const}_J T)$, naturally in both variables: a map on the left restricts to the cocone maps, and a compatible family on the right has a unique extension to the colimit. Thus colimit is left adjoint to the constant-diagram functor. If a model structure on diagrams makes the constant functor preserve fibrations and trivial fibrations, a lifting square for the colimit of a diagram (trivial) cofibration corresponds under this bijection to a lifting square against a constant (trivial) fibration. The model lifting axioms therefore make colimit preserve cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. The ordinary weak-equivalence clause of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] then makes colimit preserve weak equivalences between cofibrant diagrams. Colimit also preserves cofibrant objects, since it preserves initial objects and cofibrations.

source.place: Corollary 5.1.6 and the adjunction argument in the proof of Lemma 5.2.6, printed pp. 123 and 127.

proof.text: For (a), give the discrete category on the small index set degree zero and only identity positive and negative arrows. Apply [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Every latching object is initial and every matching object terminal; hence diagram cofibrancy is precisely component cofibrancy and diagram fibrations and trivial fibrations are objectwise. Constant diagrams therefore preserve these two right classes. Step 1 gives the weak equivalence between the coproducts and their cofibrancy. For the empty index set the diagram category has one object, its colimit is initial, and its comparison map is the identity; its initial map is an identity and thus a cofibration by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure].

source.place: Definition 5.1.1, Theorem 5.1.3 and Corollary 5.1.6, printed pp. 120-123.

proof.text: For (b), use the mixed Reedy structure on the walking span: its objects $x,a,b$ have degrees $0,1,2$, its negative nonidentity arrow is $a\to x$, and its positive nonidentity arrow is $a\to b$. Each arrow has a unique negative-then-positive factorization. By [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], the latching objects at $x,a,b$ are respectively initial, initial, and $A$. Thus a cofibrant diagram is exactly a span with $X,A$ cofibrant and $A\to B$ a cofibration; in particular each span in (b) is cofibrant. The matching objects at $x,b$ are terminal and that at $a$ is $X$. For a constant transformation on a map $p:U\to V$, the relative matching maps at $x,b$ are $p$ and at $a$ are the isomorphism $U\to V\times_V U$. Isomorphisms belong to either right lifting class by taking a diagonal with their inverse, and are weak equivalences by the model axioms. Hence the constant functor preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations. Step 1 now proves the pushout comparison, since the span transformation is an objectwise weak equivalence. Independently, $X\to X\amalg_A B$ is the pushout of $i$, hence is a cofibration by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]; composing with the initial map of $X$ proves cofibrancy. The same calculation with $X',i'$ proves the second cofibrancy assertion. No condition on $A\to X$ or $A'\to X'$ was used.

source.place: Lemma 5.2.6 and its mixed Reedy proof, printed pp. 126-127.

proof.text: For (c), use the ordinal latching objects and relative maps from [lem-coef-ordinal-latching-diagram-lifting]. Fix $\mathcal L=C={}^{\square}(F\cap W)$ or $\mathcal L=C\cap W={}^{\square}F$ by [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. If every relative latching map lies in $\mathcal L$, then for an objectwise map in the corresponding right class the child node applies at every ordinal stage and supplies a natural diagonal. No continuity of the four diagrams is used.

source.place: Definition 5.1.1, Proposition 5.1.4 and Corollary 5.1.5, printed pp. 120-122; transfinite lifts and both right classes expanded.

proof.text: For a square from $\operatorname{colim}f$ to a ground right-class map $p:U\to V$, compose its horizontal arrows with the colimit coprojections. These give a natural square from $f$ to the constant diagram on $p$. Step 4 supplies a natural diagonal $h:E\to\operatorname{const}U$. By [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], its cocone induces $H:\operatorname{colim}E\to U$. Both diagonal equations for $H$ hold after composition with every coprojection, because $h_\alpha f_\alpha=s_\alpha$ and $p h_\alpha=t_\alpha$; uniqueness in the colimit universal property proves the equations. Since $p$ was arbitrary, $\operatorname{colim}f\in\mathcal L$.

source.place: Definition 5.1.1, Proposition 5.1.4 and Corollary 5.1.5, printed pp. 120-122; transfinite lifts and both right classes expanded.

proof.text: For $\beta<\alpha<\theta$, restricting a diagram to $\alpha$ leaves exactly the same objects $\gamma<\beta$ and arrows between them. Thus its predecessor diagram at $\beta$ is unchanged. The universal property in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] identifies its latching objects, structure maps and pushout relative latching map with those defined in [lem-coef-ordinal-latching-diagram-lifting]. Apply steps 4 and 5 on the ordinal $\alpha$: they give $L_\alpha f\in\mathcal L$. This includes $\alpha=0$, where the predecessor diagram is empty and $L_0 f$ is the identity of the initial object.

source.place: Definition 5.1.1, Proposition 5.1.4 and Corollary 5.1.5, printed pp. 120-122; transfinite lifts and both right classes expanded.

proof.text: Construct both functorial factorizations of an arbitrary transformation $f:D\to E$ by transfinite recursion. Suppose $D\xrightarrow{i}Z\xrightarrow{p}E$ is already defined below $\alpha$. Form $P_\alpha=D_\alpha\amalg_{L_\alpha D}L_\alpha Z$. Its map to $E_\alpha$ is $f_\alpha$ on $D_\alpha$ and the cocone obtained from $p_\beta$ on $Z_\beta$ for $\beta<\alpha$; agreement on $L_\alpha D$ follows from $p_\beta i_\beta=f_\beta$. Factor $P_\alpha\to E_\alpha$ in the ground WFS $(C,F\cap W)$, or respectively $(C\cap W,F)$, of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. Take its middle object as $Z_\alpha$, its second map as $p_\alpha$, and its first map after $D_\alpha\to P_\alpha$ as $i_\alpha$. Define every transition $Z_\beta\to Z_\alpha$ through the coprojection $Z_\beta\to L_\alpha Z$. The latching cocone equations give the composition laws; the two factorization equations give naturality of $i,p$ and $pi=f$. In degree zero both latching objects are initial, so this is the ground factorization of $f_0$. At a limit of the recursion retain all previously defined objects and arrows; every composable pair already lies in one earlier stage. Functoriality follows because a square between transformations induces a square between the displayed maps $P_\alpha\to E_\alpha$ by the colimit and pushout universal properties, and ground factorizations are functorial. The identity and composition laws hold on all coprojections and hence on $P_\alpha$, and then on $Z_\alpha$ by ground functoriality. This produces factors with all $\lambda_\alpha(i)$ in the chosen left class and $p$ objectwise in its right class.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 5.1.3, printed pp. 122-123; both functorial factorizations expanded at zero, successor, and limit stages.

proof.text: The relative $C\cap W$ maps are exactly the relative $C$ maps that are objectwise in $W$. If all $\lambda_\alpha(f)$ are in $C\cap W$, step 6 on each predecessor segment shows $L_\alpha f\in C\cap W$. Its pushout $D_\alpha\to P_\alpha=D_\alpha\amalg_{L_\alpha D}L_\alpha E$ is in $C\cap W$ by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]; composition with $\lambda_\alpha(f)$ shows $f_\alpha\in C\cap W$. Conversely suppose $f$ is relative $C$ and objectwise in $W$. Induct on $\alpha$ that $\lambda_\alpha(f)\in C\cap W$. The induction hypothesis and step 6 on the predecessor segment make $L_\alpha f$ a trivial cofibration. Pushout closure makes $D_\alpha\to P_\alpha$ trivial. Since $f_\alpha$ is its composite with $\lambda_\alpha(f)$, two-out-of-three gives $\lambda_\alpha(f)\in W$; it is already in $C$. The base $\alpha=0$ uses the identity on the initial object for $L_0f$, which belongs to both left classes by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. This same reasoning applies at every limit ordinal because step 6 already covers its whole predecessor segment. The forward argument with $C$ in place of $C\cap W$ also proves that relative $C$ maps are objectwise cofibrations.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 5.1.3 and Remark 5.1.7, printed pp. 122-123; both directions and the limit stage written out.

proof.text: Put $W_\theta,F_\theta$ equal to the objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations, and $C_\theta$ equal to the maps with all relative latching maps in $C$. Limits and colimits of diagrams are computed objectwise: maps between the component (co)limits are induced by the diagram arrows, their composition laws follow by equality on every projection or coprojection, and the component universal properties identify cones or cocones in the functor category. Thus this category is complete and cocomplete. The class $W_\theta$ satisfies two-out-of-three and is retract closed componentwise. Relative left classes are retract closed because $f\mapsto\lambda_\alpha(f)$ is a functor on arrow categories, so takes retract diagrams to retract diagrams, and the ground left classes are retract closed by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. Objectwise right classes are retract closed by the right-class part of that node. Steps 4 and 7 give lifting and functorial factorizations for (relative $C$, objectwise $F\cap W$) and (relative $C\cap W$, objectwise $F$). They give mutual lifting characterizations too: factoring a map that lifts against every right-class map makes it a retract of its left factor, by the diagonal of the factorization square; factoring a map against which all left-class maps lift makes it a retract of its right factor by the other diagonal. The retract closures just checked put those maps in the indicated classes. These are therefore two WFS. By step 8 their left classes are $C_\theta$ and $C_\theta\cap W_\theta$, while the right classes are $F_\theta\cap W_\theta$ and $F_\theta$. This verifies every model-category axiom in [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], with functorial factorizations, for all $\theta$-diagrams.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 5.1.3, printed pp. 122-123; retract and model-axiom checks supplied instead of invoking the theorem as an uncited fact.

proof.text: In the model structure proved in steps 4-9, the constant functor preserves fibrations and trivial fibrations because these are objectwise classes. Step 1 therefore applies to $\operatorname{colim}_{\alpha<\theta}$. For a chain $X$ in (c), the latching map at zero is the cofibrant initial map. At a successor $\alpha=\beta+1$ the predecessor category has terminal object $\beta$, so its colimit is $X_\beta$ by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and its latching map is the assumed successor cofibration. At a nonzero limit $\alpha<\theta$, continuity makes $L_\alpha X\to X_\alpha$ an isomorphism, hence a cofibration: its inverse supplies every lift. Thus $X$ is cofibrant in this diagram model category. Applying these three checks to $Y$ proves its diagram cofibrancy. The transformation $u$ is in $W_\theta$ by its assumed component weak equivalences, so step 1 proves the colimit comparison and cofibrancy of both colimits. All constructions used only the two ground WFS, two-out-of-three, retract closure, and the displayed colimits. In particular, no properness hypothesis is needed in (a), (b), or (c).

lean.statement: theorem modelCofibrantColimitComparison (M : Type u) [Category.{v} M] [ModelCategory M] [HasLimits M] [HasColimits M] [HasLimitsOfSize.{w, w} M] [HasColimitsOfSize.{w, w} M] [(cofibrations M).HasFunctorialFactorization (trivialFibrations M)] [(trivialCofibrations M).HasFunctorialFactorization (fibrations M)] : (∀ (I : Type w) (F G : Discrete I ⥤ M) (f : F ⟶ G), (∀ i : Discrete I, IsCofibrant (F.obj i)) → (∀ i : Discrete I, IsCofibrant (G.obj i)) → (∀ i : Discrete I, WeakEquivalence (f.app i)) → WeakEquivalence (colimMap f) ∧ IsCofibrant (colimit F) ∧ IsCofibrant (colimit G)) ∧ (∀ (S T : WalkingSpan ⥤ M) (f : S ⟶ T), (∀ j : WalkingSpan, IsCofibrant (S.obj j)) → (∀ j : WalkingSpan, IsCofibrant (T.obj j)) → Cofibration (S.map WalkingSpan.Hom.snd) → Cofibration (T.map WalkingSpan.Hom.snd) → (∀ j : WalkingSpan, WeakEquivalence (f.app j)) → WeakEquivalence (colimMap f) ∧ IsCofibrant (colimit S) ∧ IsCofibrant (colimit T)) ∧ (∀ (θ : Type w) [LinearOrder θ] [OrderBot θ] [SuccOrder θ] [NoMaxOrder θ] [WellFoundedLT θ] (X Y : θ ⥤ M) (f : X ⟶ Y), IsCofibrant (X.obj ⊥) → IsCofibrant (Y.obj ⊥) → (∀ α : θ, Cofibration (X.map (homOfLE (Order.le_succ α)))) → (∀ α : θ, Cofibration (Y.map (homOfLE (Order.le_succ α)))) → X.IsWellOrderContinuous → Y.IsWellOrderContinuous → (∀ α : θ, WeakEquivalence (f.app α)) → WeakEquivalence (colimMap f) ∧ IsCofibrant (colimit X) ∧ IsCofibrant (colimit Y))
